body.estimand_functional: \(\theta=H/B-1=\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}(w^0_{gt}/B)(v_{gt}-1)\), with exact honest inference defined by \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\) and \(D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\)

sampling_model.design: Condition on observed \(s\in\mathcal S_T\) and on calibrated, known \(\kappa>0\); require honesty uniformly over the entire observed-share simplex.
sampling_model.units: The observations are the fixed collection of cohort--time totals \(X_{gt}\), not an individual-level sample or a finite-population randomization.
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort \(g\) is untreated for \(t<g\) and treated for \(t\ge g\); the never-treated cohort is indexed by \(\infty\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cohort share is at least \(1/(2T)\). The exposure, time-effect, and treated-multiplier boxes are separately maintained restrictions on the aggregate-Poisson experiment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-count inference profiles \(A,b,v\) exactly under the product-Poisson likelihood. The high-intensity bridge estimates normalized row and time effects from untreated cells and treated totals. Estimating or jointly calibrating an unknown intensity is not covered.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The estimator uses the ratio of average observed and counterfactual outcomes.
Pooled canonical-link quasi-likelihood and imputation produce identical cohort-time estimates under the stated nonlinear parallel-trends model.
Fixed-effect averages are consistent and asymptotically normal with the cross section growing and fixed \(T\).
Minimax expected-measure confidence sets are characterized using Bayes--minimax duality.
Theorem 6 controls off-support maximum risk while the finite-prior Monte Carlo procedure converges to its game value.
The scalar Poisson interval cannot be shortened without lowering infimal coverage below its nominal level.
Auxiliary-uniform randomization splits binomial atoms and yields exact equi-tailed intervals.
An optimal interval is obtained for a single parameter in a discrete distribution under mean criteria.
Section 2 establishes uniform asymptotic size through behavior along qualitative drifting subsequences.
Explicit randomized mappings establish global asymptotic equivalence between positive Poisson and Gaussian experiments.

body.tldr: A staggered multiplicative panel with rare Poisson totals turns the Moreau--Kastler equation (3.14) proportional-effect setup into a discrete minimax confidence problem. The contribution derives the exact low-intensity deterministic value and all optimizers, proves a strict first-order gain from randomized interval kernels, prices the stronger all-untreated-zero fallback separately, and relates both procedures to the efficient high-intensity Gaussian limit. Its central open theorem asks for an exact finite machine representation: rational polyhedral cells, endpoint-grid policy tables, outward-rounded Poisson enclosures, and a terminating verifier whose acceptance proves global share--intensity honesty and a complete integer lower bound. The mandatory \(T=3\), \(\alpha=.05\), \(\kappa=.01\), \(K=2\), and \(h=.01\) instance must close the certified gap within \(.05\).

project_justification.gap: Regular staggered-PPML work supplies the proportional target and high-information inference, while exact discrete interval work treats scalar families or finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations. Schafer and Stark (2009) do not provide deterministic finite termination or continuum honesty, and Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020) do not turn qualitative drifting subsequences into a finite verifiable cover.
project_justification.niche: The nonregular object is the entire worst-nuisance expected-length frontier, with deterministic connected intervals, randomized kernels, and the all-untreated-zero restriction kept distinct under maintained aggregate-exposure boxes and calibrated known intensity.
project_justification.fill: The paper joins exact low-count values and a high-count efficiency bridge to a finite certificate format whose accepted rational data prove global coverage, a conservative upper risk, and an integrality-preserving lower bound with an explicit error ledger.

body.related_work: Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), supplies the imputed counterfactual-share proportional target; that algebraic specialization is setup rather than a novel theorem here. Wooldridge (2023) identifies staggered nonlinear cohort-time effects and makes pooled Poisson quasi-likelihood operational under fixed \(T\), while Martin (2017), Theorems 1--2, establishes regular fixed-\(T\) asymptotics for multiplicative-panel averages; both inform the high-information endpoint. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005), Theorem 1, supplies Bayes--minimax duality but does not calculate this multivariate connected-interval game. Kabaila and Byrne (2001) supply the ordered scalar exact-Poisson benchmark and the homogeneous known-mass reduction is only a sanity check. Kabaila (2013) supplies auxiliary-uniform atom splitting, and Habiger, McCann, and Tebbs (2013) studies integrated one-parameter discrete optimality. Schafer and Stark (2009), especially Theorem 6 and the Conclusion, establish finite-prior Monte Carlo convergence and off-support risk control, but not a deterministic stopping rule, global continuum honesty, or a complete integer lower certificate. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, characterize uniform asymptotic size through drifting subsequences, but do not provide finite rational cells, computable outward enclosures, or a terminating acceptance predicate. The open certificate question is stated as a strict finite verified strengthening of these last two guarantees. Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004), Theorems 1 and 3, informs the Poisson--Gaussian comparison without itself profiling this causal nuisance or transferring the connected-interval minimax game.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The presolve calculations are evidence, not established results. The mandatory early-kill instance is \(T=3\), \(\alpha=.05\), \(\kappa=.01\), count box \(K=2\), and endpoint mesh \(.01\): it must produce an accepted globally share-uniform deterministic primal and a complete integer lower certificate with gap at most \(.05\). A nuisance grid, sampled-share check, fixed-share certificate, root linear-programming relaxation, or unbudgeted numerical gap does not pass. Exact real-exponential contacts may defeat naive algebraic stopping, so termination of the finite verifier construction remains the load-bearing open issue.
body.honest_scope: All contribution statements are to be proved. The causal-functional identity is setup credited to Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), and the homogeneous known-mass scalar reduction is a sanity check credited to Kabaila and Byrne (2001). The independent Poisson total law and share lower bound define the experiment; the exposure, time-effect, treatment-effect, and calibrated known-intensity restrictions are maintained rather than consequences of PPML theory. An unknown or estimated intensity changes the experiment and remains unsolved. No claim is made for noninteger outcomes, arbitrary overdispersion, individual-data sufficiency, or software-default intervals. The exact positive-intensity randomized value away from the low-count phase and the global closed-form maximizer of \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\) are outside the promised theorem spine unless they emerge from the certificate analysis.
